title: OpenAI Raises $11B at $1.25T Valuation, Falls Far Short of $30B Target
summary: OpenAI raised $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, falling short of its $30 billion target after an AI-sector selloff. Here is what the funding gap means for builders and developers on OpenAI platform.

OpenAI Funding


# OpenAI Raises $11B at $1.25T Valuation, Falls Far Short of $30B Target


By OpenTools Team


·


November 8, 2026


OpenAI closed the first $11 billion of a funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion — less than half the $30 billion it originally targeted. The scaled‑back raise, confirmed by CFO Sarah Friar, comes as AI stocks tumbled following the midterm elections and investor appetite for big‑ticket AI bets shows signs of cooling. For builders and developers relying on OpenAI's platform, the funding gap raises questions about the pace of future model releases and infrastructure investment.


## The $30B Ask Became an $11B Close


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) wired roughly $11 billion into its accounts by Friday, November 6, 2026, marking the first close of a funding round that values the ChatGPT maker at $1.25 trillion pre-money, according to[Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/openai-completes-11-billion-portion-of-funding-at-1-25-trillion-value) . That is less than half of the $30 billion the company originally aimed to raise — and well below the $1.4 to $1.5 trillion valuation two investors told[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/openai-just-raised-11-billion-133842228.html) OpenAI initially sought.


CFO Sarah Friar confirmed the $1.25 trillion figure in a TV interview but pushed back on reports of a higher starting price, saying the $1.4 trillion number "started with a media report and never came from OpenAI." The round could still grow to as much as $20 billion in the coming weeks, with a second tranche of up to $9 billion yet to close.


SoftBank and Abu Dhabi's MGX participated in this first close. Other investors include Coatue Management, T. Rowe Price, Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Andreessen Horowitz, and a United Arab Emirates consortium, per[The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/openai-lands-an-11-billion-funding-round-but-has-to-court-dentists-for-more-capital/) .


## Why the Numbers Shrank: An AI Stock Rout and Midterm Jolt


The funding pullback did not happen in a vacuum. An AI-linked stock selloff swept markets this week after Democrats won control in the US midterm elections, with many candidates having campaigned on slowing data center construction. The Nasdaq 100 shed 6.4% on Thursday before recovering somewhat on Friday, according to[The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-pushes-ahead-with-pre-thanksgiving-ipo-despite-tech-selloff-accepts-lower-valuation/) .


Voters rejected data center ballot measures in 40 of 41 local contests across 10 states, as[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/data-center-ballot-measures-2026-midterm.html) tallied. The sole exception was Harwood, North Dakota. "The midterms were not about stopping data centers, but putting checks on them,"[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/06/midterm-elections-ai-data-center-build-out-social-license/) reported.


In response,[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) published a National Community Compact on Thursday pledging to cover electricity and[grid](https://opentools.ai/tools/grid) infrasructure costs for data center campuses it owns and operates, and to post financial guarantees before major spending begins — moves Fortune described as OpenAI seeking a "social license" to build.


## The March Comparison: Then $122B, Now a Harder Sell


Eight months ago,[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) raised $122 billion at an $852 billion valuation in a March 2026 round that was oversubscribed. The contrast is stark. "If OpenAI is already courting dentists to scrape together more capital, it tells you the AI funding market is either tapped out or too concentrated on OpenAI and[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) ," wrote[The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/openai-lands-an-11-billion-funding-round-but-has-to-court-dentists-for-more-capital/) , noting that OpenAI is working with investment banks to bring in wealthy individual investors to close the gap.


Friar claimed OpenAI's business grew 70% quarter over quarter, a figure she offered as evidence the company's fundamentals remain strong despite the cooler fundraising climate. But for existing shareholders like **[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft)** and **NVIDIA** , the valuation haircut matters: both companies depend on OpenAI's ability to fund its ambitious infrastructure plans.


## The Anthropic Shadow: IPO Valuation Also Under Pressure


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) is not alone in feeling the chill.[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) , the creator of Claude and OpenAI's chief rival, is pushing ahead with its own pre-Thanksgiving IPO but has also accepted a lower valuation. Investors now estimate Anthropic's public market value at $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion, down from the $2 trillion floated just weeks ago, according to the[Financial Times](https://www.ft.com/content/314e17df-e7af-4814-b208-70a0557cb452) . Some investors, rattled by the tech selloff, have floated figures as low as $1.1 trillion, per[Billionaires.Africa](https://www.billionaires.africa/2026/11/07/american-billionaire-dario-amodeis-anthropic-ipo-valuation-could-fall-to-1-1-trillion-after-ai-stock-rout/) . Anthropic aims to raise $80-100 billion in the offering.


Anthropic's annualized revenue sits at approximately $81 billion, up from $65 billion at the end of July, per[The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/anthropic-pushes-ahead-with-pre-thanksgiving-ipo-despite-tech-selloff-accepts-lower-valuation/) . Its[amended S-1 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026068676/anthropicpbc-sx1ax1.htm) from November 2 disclosed approximately $895.4 billion in purchase commitments and lease agreements, substantially all for compute and infrastructure.


## What This Means for Builders


The funding shortfall does not mean[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) is running out of money — $11 billion is still the largest AI funding tranche in history. But the gap between ambition ($30B) and reality ($11B) suggests the era of blank-check AI fundraising may be ending. For developers building on OpenAI's platform, there are several implications:


- **Pricing pressure:** OpenAI may need to show faster revenue growth to close the full $20 billion round, which could accelerate enterprise pricing changes or API rate limit adjustments.
- **Model release cadence:** Infrastructure investment — the primary use of these funds — directly affects how quickly new models can be trained and deployed. A leaner round means harder prioritization.
- **Competitive landscape:**[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's concurrent IPO means both major AI labs will soon face quarterly earnings scrutiny. Public market pressure historically drives both innovation and cost-cutting — builders should watch for shifts in free tier limits, API pricing, and model availability.
- **Data center politics:** The midterm results signal that communities want a say in where AI infrastructure gets built. OpenAI's community compact is a recognition that capital alone is not enough — permission matters too. Builders deploying AI workloads at scale should factor in potential regional constraints on compute availability.


## The Bigger Picture: AI Capital Recalibration


The simultaneous cooling of both[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's private raise and[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's IPO expectations, combined with a broad tech selloff and voter pushback on data centers, suggests a broader recalibration. "Two days after voters rejected data centers almost everywhere, OpenAI went shopping for something it cannot build: permission,"[Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/06/midterm-elections-ai-data-center-build-out-social-license/) wrote.


The AI industry is not out of money — far from it. But the cost of capital is rising, and the political license to build is getting harder to earn. For the first time since ChatGPT launched, AI companies are learning that growth at any cost has a ceiling.
